extracted.intended_audience: developers and contributors to the Sage (SageMath) project (code, docs, packages)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for contributing code, documentation, tests, and packages to the Sage (SageMath) project via Git/GitHub, including coding conventions, testing, packaging, and PR workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable contribution types
rubrics_metrics.description: Everybody who uses Sage is encouraged to contribute something back to Sage at some point. You could: Add examples to the documentation; Find bugs or typos; Fix a bug; Implement a new function or create a new class; Contribute a useful tutorial for a mathematical topic; Translate an existing document to a new language; Upgrade a package, create a fast new C library, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enumerates the kinds of contributions welcomed: documentation examples, bug reports/fixes, new code/classes, tutorials, translations, package upgrades, C libraries, and similar improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain and build Sage source before contributing
rubrics_metrics.description: To begin with, you need of course your own copy of Sage source code to change it. Use our Installation guide to get the source code and build Sage from source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay close attention to prerequisites to build on your platform, especially if you have never worked on software before.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Git for revision control
rubrics_metrics.description: To share changes with the Sage community, you need to learn about revision control. We use the software Git for this purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide walks through setting up Git on your platform and preparing a local branch to share with all Sage users; see detailed Git sections for tricky situations such as merge conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use GitHub and the Sage repository workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: All changes go through the Sage repository on GitHub at some point. It contains bug reports, enhancement proposals, changes in progress, and all the history of Sage today. You have to be familiar with it to be involved in Sage development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes forking the repo, linking Git to your GitHub account, using the GitHub CLI, opening issues and pull requests, and commenting on issues/PRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Gitpod as an easy development environment (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: As an easy way to get started, you can run and edit Sage’s code and contribute your changes using Gitpod, a free online development environment based on VS Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gitpod launches a pre-made workspace with dependencies and tools installed; read the Gitpod guidelines and Gitpod-specific notes for development and using pre-built Docker images for VS Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Branching and PR workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Branching out, preparing a local branch, making commits, and opening a pull request are the standard workflow for sharing changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections cover creating a new PR, checking out an existing PR, uploading more changes, finishing a PR, merging the upstream develop branch, and the general development workflow at a glance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making commits and commit hygiene
rubrics_metrics.description: Making commits is a distinct step: prepare commits that represent your changes clearly and correctly before opening a PR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide contains guidance on commit-making; see also 'rewriting history' and 'interactively rebasing' for polishing commit history when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checks on pull requests / automated checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Pull requests are subject to automated checks and status; Documentation Previews and other checks help validate changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The repo uses GitHub Actions, buildbots, and other CI to test PRs; contributors should ensure their PRs pass relevant checks before merging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing changes locally before submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Every change of Sage source code has a risk to break Sage, and must be tested before being merged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Testing Sage section explains tools and workflows for running doctests, testing a module, troubleshooting, parallel testing many modules or the whole library, and doctesting from within Sage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Run and maintain doctests
rubrics_metrics.description: Running Sage’s doctests is a central testing mechanism: developers should run doctests for modules they change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes running doctests, using the doctest fixer, running doctests with Coverage.py, and doctesting from within Sage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test on multiple platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Testing on multiple platforms is required/encouraged to ensure changes do not break Sage across environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use GitHub Actions, Sage buildbots, pre-built Docker images, or other multi-platform testing strategies described in the guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use CI tools and test reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Testing PRs with GitHub Actions and obtaining test reports on sage-release are part of the validation process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide enumerates CI tools (GitHub Actions, buildbots) and how to interpret and act on test reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel and large-scale testing
rubrics_metrics.description: There are procedures for parallel testing many modules or the whole Sage library when changes are large or wide-reaching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide describes how to run parallel testing locally and on infrastructure, and how to troubleshoot failures that appear only under parallel execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing and closing PRs
rubrics_metrics.description: PRs are reviewed by maintainers; contributors should be prepared for code review and subsequent changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections include 'Reviewing Code', 'Reviewing and closing PRs', 'Reasons to invalidate PRs', and commenting etiquette on issues and PRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons to invalidate PRs
rubrics_metrics.description: There are explicit reasons that can cause a PR to be invalidated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintainers may close or invalidate PRs for policy violations, failing checks, poor quality tests/documentation, or other stated reasons in the PR workflow section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merging and release process
rubrics_metrics.description: The guide describes the release process and how PRs get merged into develop and released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes steps for finishing PRs, merging upstream develop branch, and the broader release process used by the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Git basics and advanced Git operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on Git basics (authentication through SSH, pushing changes, checking out PRs, getting changes from remotes) and advanced topics (merge/rebase, detached heads, rewriting history, interactive rebase, reset and recovery).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these procedures when resolving merge conflicts, updating branches, or preparing clean commit histories; the guide includes tips, merge tools, and best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workspace setup and recommended editors/IDEs
rubrics_metrics.description: Set up your workspace with recommended text editors and IDEs for use with Sage; guidance on Gitpod and VS Code integration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose supported editors/IDEs and configure them per the guide to improve productivity and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Python code style and conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: A guide on conventions in writing code and documentation; including Python code style, Python version, files and directory structure, docstrings, whitespace style, and other general coding style notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A beginning developer should read this to be a good developer; conventions evolve and experienced developers should review this chapter periodically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation strings and running automated doctests
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation strings (docstrings) should be written so they can be tested via doctests; automated doctests are part of validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the docstring style guidance and ensure examples in docstrings are correct and testable.

rubrics_metrics.name: General coding style regarding whitespace and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the project's general coding style concerning whitespace and formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use linters and style tools (pycodestyle, ruff) listed in the guide to enforce formatting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use static analysis and linters
rubrics_metrics.description: The guide lists development and testing tools such as pycodestyle, Cython-lint, ruff, relint, codespell, pyflakes, pyright, pytest, and act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run appropriate linters and static analysis tools and fix reported issues before submitting PRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing tools and coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Doctest with Coverage.py and other tools to measure and maintain test coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure changes are adequately covered by tests and check coverage reports as part of CI and local testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing and updating the manuals/documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: All features of Sage are documented in the manuals. This part explains the technical aspect of updating Sage documentation: editing the documentation, hyperlinks, adding a new file, and building the manuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributors changing features must also update the manuals and ensure docs build correctly; documentation previews help validate changes on PRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Syntax highlighting and Cython documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuals support syntax highlighting for Cython code and have guidance for documenting Cython-specific code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When documenting Cython code, follow the syntax-highlighting and doc-building guidance to ensure correct rendering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding in Python for Sage — design and special functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on Python language standard, design, special Sage functions, LaTeX and print representations, conversion to matrix/vector, and Sage-specific behaviors (preparsing, coercion model, mutability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Sage-specific API/design rules (e.g., print/LaTeX methods, coercion/mutability rules) when implementing new classes or functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementing __hash__ and mutability rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The guide addresses the __hash__ special method and rules around mutability for Sage objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure objects implement hashing correctly and follow mutability conventions to avoid subtle bugs (details in the 'More on Coding for Sage' section).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception handling and integer return values
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on how to handle exceptions and the expectation for integer return values where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow project norms for exceptions and return-value conventions to maintain API consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Static typing and deprecation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice on static typing, deprecation, experimental/unstable code, and how to mark or handle deprecated or experimental features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the project's deprecation procedures when removing or changing behavior; mark experimental features clearly and provide migration paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using optional packages and external libraries/interfaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on using optional packages and interfaces to external systems such as PARI, GAP, LibGAP, and Singular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified interfaces, attachment/loading patterns, and inclusion rules for external libraries; see sections on each supported interface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding in Cython and related constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on writing Cython code in Sage, attaching or loading .spyx files, interrupt and signal handling, unpickling Cython code, and Cython-specific deprecation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Cython coding guidelines and unpickling/serialization rules to ensure safety and portability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packaging third-party code for Sage
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for packaging third-party code: package types, directory structure, utility scripts to create and maintain packages, building the package, modifying third-party code, and the inclusion procedure for new and updated packages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the inclusion procedure and packaging guidelines before adding or updating third-party packages in Sage; test distribution packages and their dependencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packaging SageMath downstream and dependencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for packaging Sage downstream: dependencies, build procedure, example downstream packages, modularized distribution, modules/packages/distribution packages, and hierarchy of distribution packages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure downstream packaging follows the project's dependency and distribution model; test distribution packages thoroughly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing distribution packages and indices
rubrics_metrics.description: Testing distribution packages and maintaining indices and tables for packaged modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the testing recommendations for distribution packages and update indices/tables as required by packaging procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use project-provided development and testing tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Use recommended dev tools: uv, Tox, Doctest, Coverage.py, startuptime, Pycodestyle, Cython-lint, Ruff, Relint, Codespell, Pytest, Pyright, Pyflakes, Act, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run and integrate these tools into your development workflow to catch issues early and to conform to project standards.
